Since V on arrows quantifies over arguments u1,u2 and requires E of applications, and applications reduce to `tm_protect κ.ir (open body u)`, we need a lemma: if bodies are related under related substitutions, then after opening with related values they're related. This is the standard "open" lemma for locally nameless LRs: `V l T1 u1 u2 -> E ... (open body1 u1) (open body2 u2)` given that body1/body2 are "related under any related substitution" — proved by using fresh variable and substituting values via a substitution lemma.

This is going to be a substantial development: substitution lemmas for open/subst, renaming, etc. In locally nameless with tm_fvar atoms and Nat.eqb-based subst, we need:
- `subst` lemmas (commutation, etc.)
- `open` and `subst` interaction: open body (tm_fvar x) under x fresh; substituting a value for x gives... We need to relate `open body u` with substitution. Standard approach: prove `subst x v (open body (tm_fvar x)) = open body v` when x not free in body — actually careful: open replaces bvar 0 with fvar x; subst replaces fvar x with v. If x ∉ fv body, then subst x v (open body (fvar x)) = open body v? Let's check: open body (fvar x) replaces all tm_bvar 0 with fvar x. Then subst x v replaces fvar x occurrences with v. The result has v at those positions. open body v replaces bvar 0 with v directly. Since subst doesn't touch bvars (subst on tm_bvar i = tm_bvar i), and the body's free bvars are 0 under binders... Wait open body v = open_rec 0 v body, which replaces bvar 0 with v everywhere except under binders where the index is incremented. Fixpoint V (l : label) (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop :=
 match T with
 | Ty_Unit κ => fun v1 v2 => True
 | Ty_Sum T1 T2 κ => fun v1 v2 => if visb κ l then (shape...) else True
 | Ty_Prod T1 T2 κ => ...
 | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 κ => fun f1 f2 => if visb κ l then
      forall u1 u2 r, flows_to κ.reader r -> V l T1 u1 u2 ->
        forall w1 w2, tm_app f1 u1 r -->* w1 -> tm_app f2 u2 r -->* w2 -> 
          V_prot l κ.ir T2 w1 w2
    else True
 end

where V_prot l l0 T is V but with T's top annotation joined with l0. Definitions:

```
Definition flowsb (l1 l2 : label) : bool :=
  match l1, l2 with High, Low => false | _, _ => true end.

Lemma flowsb_iff : forall l1 l2, flowsb l1 l2 = true <-> flows_to l1 l2.
```

Define:
```
Fixpoint VR (l : label) (T : ty) (top : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 : tm),
            v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\ VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2)
        \/ (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 : tm),
            v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\ VR l T2 (security_of T2) u1 u2)
      else True
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists k1 k2 u1 u2 w1 w2,
           v1 = tm_pair u1 w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair u2 w2 k2 /\
           VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2 /\ VR l T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2)
      else True
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (forall (u1 u2 : tm) (r : label),
            flows_to top.(reader) r ->
            VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2 ->
            forall w1 w2, tm_app v1 u1 r -->* w1 -> tm_app v2 u2 r -->* w2 ->
              VR l T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) top.(indirect_reader)) w1 w2)
      else True
  end.

Definition V (l : label) (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop := VR l T (security_of T).
```

Let me now write the full definition:

```
Fixpoint VR (l : label) (T : ty) (top : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 : tm),
           v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
           VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2)
        \/ (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 : tm),
           v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
           VR l T2 (security_of T2) u1 u2)
      else True
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 w1 w2 : tm),
           v1 = tm_pair u1 w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair u2 w2 k2 /\
           security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
           VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2 /\
           VR l T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2)
      else True
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        match v1, v2 with
        | tm_abs _ body1 k1, tm_abs _ body2 k2 =>
            security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
            (forall (l1 l2 : label) (u1 u2 : tm) (r : label),
               flows_to top.(reader) r ->
               VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2 ->
               forall w1 w2,
                 tm_protect (join k1.(indirect_reader) l1) (open body1 u1) -->* w1 ->
                 tm_protect (join k2.(indirect_reader) l2) (open body2 u2) -->* w2 ->
                 VR l T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) (join top.(indirect_reader) (join l1 l2))) w1 w2)
        | _, _ => True
        end
      else True
  end.
```

Now the subst_env lemmas. Define:

```
Fixpoint subst_env (rho : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => rho x
  | tm_unit k => tm_unit k
  | tm_abs T body k => tm_abs T (subst_env rho body) k
  | tm_app t1 t2 r => tm_app (subst_env rho t1) (subst_env rho t2) r
  | tm_pair t1 t2 k => tm_pair (subst_env rho t1) (subst_env rho t2) k
  | tm_fst t1 r => tm_fst (subst_env rho t1) r
  | tm_snd t1 r => tm_snd (subst_env rho t1) r
  | tm_inl t1 k => tm_inl (subst_env rho t1) k
  | tm_inr t1 k => tm_inr (subst_env rho t1) k
  | tm_case t0 b1 b2 r => tm_case (subst_env rho t0) (subst_env rho b1) (subst_env rho b2) r
  | tm_protect l t1 => tm_protect l (subst_env rho t1)
  | tm_if c y n r => tm_if (subst_env rho c) (subst_env rho y) (subst_env rho n) r
  end.
```

- Prod/Arrow ✓ (arrow components also).

Now the VR definition. Let me write it:

```coq
Definition flowsb (l1 l2 : label) : bool :=
  match l1, l2 with High, Low => false | _, _ => true end.

Lemma flowsb_true : forall l1 l2, flowsb l1 l2 = true <-> flows_to l1 l2.
Proof. intros; destruct l1,l2; simpl; intuition discriminate. Qed.

Lemma flowsb_false : forall l1 l2, flowsb l1 l2 = false <-> ~ flows_to l1 l2.
Proof. intros; destruct l1,l2; simpl; intuition discriminate. Qed.
```

Then:
```coq
Fixpoint VR (l : label) (T : ty) (top : security) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists k1 k2 : security, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2)
      else True
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 : tm),
            v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\
            security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
            VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2)
        \/ (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 : tm),
            v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\
            security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
            VR l T2 (security_of T2) u1 u2)
      else True
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        (exists (k1 k2 : security) (u1 u2 w1 w2 : tm),
            v1 = tm_pair u1 w1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair u2 w2 k2 /\
            security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
            VR l T1 (security_of T1) u1 u2 /\
            VR l T2 (security_of T2) w1 w2)
      else True
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      if flowsb top.(indirect_reader) l then
        match v1, v2 with
        | tm_abs _ body1 k1, tm_abs _ body2 k2 =>
            security_le k1 top /\ security_le k2 top /\
            (forall (u1 u2 : tm),
               (forall (v1' v2' : tm), evaluates u1 v1' -> evaluates u2 v2' ->
                  VR l T1 (security_of T1) v1' v2') ->
               locally_closed u1 -> locally_closed u2 ->
               forall (l1 l2 r : label), flows_to top.(reader) r ->
                 forall w1 w2,
                   tm_protect (join k1.(indirect_reader) l1) (open body1 u1) -->* w1 ->
                   tm_protect (join k2.(indirect_reader) l2) (open body2 u2) -->* w2 ->
                   VR l T2 (protect_security (security_of T2) (join top.(indirect_reader) (join l1 l2))) w1 w2)
        | _, _ => True
        end
      else True
  end.

Definition V (l : label) (T : ty) : tm -> tm -> Prop := VR l T (security_of T).

Definition E (l : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> V l T v1 v2.
```

Hmm, wait. There's a concern about the arrow relation's argument premise using E, which is defined after VR — since E is a Definition referencing V referencing VR, and VR doesn't reference E (I inlined the E definition), it's fine ✓.

Hmm, but the inlined E premise in VR is `forall v1' v2', evaluates u1 v1' -> evaluates u2 v2' -> VR l T1 (security_of T1) v1' v2'` ✓ structurally fine (VR at T1).

Now, the recursion check: VR's Fixpoint on T calls VR at T1 and T2 ✓, and in the arrow case, calls VR at T1 and T2 ✓ (inside the forall). Coq's guard checker should accept since T1, T2 are direct subterms ✓.

But wait: `match v1, v2 with` inside the Ty_Arrow branch with a `forall` quantifier — fine.

Definition prot_sec (T : ty) (p : label) : security := protect_security (security_of T) p.

Fixpoint val_rel (l p : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  let κ := protect_security (security_of T) p in
  flows_to κ.(indirect_reader) l ->
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => match v1, v2 with tm_unit _, tm_unit _ => True | _, _ => False end
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ => match v1, v2 with
      | tm_inl a1 _, tm_inl a2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2
      | tm_inr b1 _, tm_inr b2 _ => val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
      | _, _ => False end
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ => match v1, v2 with
      | tm_pair a1 b1 _, tm_pair a2 b2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2 /\ val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
      | _, _ => False end
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      forall w1 w2 r, value w1 -> value w2 -> val_rel l Low T1 w1 w2 ->
        flows_to κ.(reader) r -> interp l κ.(indirect_reader) T2 (tm_app v1 w1 r)(tm_app v2 w2 r)
  end
with interp (l p : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> val_rel l p T v1 v2.

So the val_rel definition:

Fixpoint val_rel (l p : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  let κ := protect_security (security_of T) p in
  flows_to κ.(indirect_reader) l ->
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => match v1, v2 with tm_unit _, tm_unit _ => True | _, _ => False end
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      match v1, v2 with
      | tm_inl a1 _, tm_inl a2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2
      | tm_inr b1 _, tm_inr b2 _ => val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
      | _, _ => False
      end
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      match v1, v2 with
      | tm_pair a1 b1 _, tm_pair a2 b2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2 /\ val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
      | _, _ => False
      end
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      value v1 -> value v2 ->
      forall (a1 a2 : tm) (r : label),
        value a1 -> value a2 -> val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2 ->
        flows_to κ.(reader) r ->
        forall u1 u2 : tm,
          evaluates (tm_app v1 a1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app v2 a2 r) u2 ->
          val_rel l κ.(indirect_reader) T2 u1 u2
  end.

For protect1/protect lemmas, protect_value of a non-unit value form could change shape only if it's a value form. If v1 is tm_pair, protect_value yields pair; but val_rel at unit would require v1 unit anyway (via match) unless obs fails. In protect1's proof: RHS val_rel at protected unit type with obs'→obs; H gives v1=unit (shape); protect_value gives unit. Fine.

Do we want val_rel at sum to additionally require values? Suppose v1 = tm_inl x κ with x non-value; relation requires val_rel at payload T1 — which may hold (e.g., obs false). Then protect_value (inl x κ) L = inl x (protect κ L); shape preserved. Fine.

Let me define:

Fixpoint fv_context (C : program_context) : list atom :=
  match C with
  | C_Hole => []
  | C_Abs _ C' _ => fv_context C'
  | C_AppLeft C' t r => fv_context C' ++ fv t
  | C_AppRight t C' r => fv t ++ fv_context C'
  | C_PairLeft C' t κ => fv_context C' ++ fv t
  | C_PairRight t C' κ => fv t ++ fv_context C'
  | C_Fst C' _ => fv_context C'
  | C_Snd C' _ => fv_context C'
  | C_Inl C' _ => fv_context C'
  | C_Inr C' _ => fv_context C'
  | C_CaseScrutinee C' b1 b2 r => fv_context C' ++ fv b1 ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseLeft t0 C' b2 r => fv t0 ++ fv_context C' ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseRight t0 b1 C' r => fv t0 ++ fv b1 ++ fv_context C'
  | C_Protect _ C' => fv_context C'
  | C_IfCondition C' y n r => fv_context C' ++ fv y ++ fv n
  | C_IfThen c C' n r => fv c ++ fv_context C' ++ fv n
  | C_IfElse c y C' r => fv c ++ fv y ++ fv_context C'
  end.

Then prove in each case that fv piece ⊆ fv_context C using `In` and `app` lemmas (List.in_app_iff / in_app_or / in_or_app). This is a bit of boilerplate but manageable.

Define vsec (v : tm) : security := match v with unit κ|abs _ _ κ|pair _ _ κ|inl _ κ|inr _ κ => κ | _ => public end.

val_rel l p T v1 v2 :=
  flows_to (join (security_of T).ir p) l ->
  security_le (vsec v1) (protect_security (security_of T) p) /\
  security_le (vsec v2) (protect_security (security_of T) p) /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ => match v1,v2 with tm_unit _, tm_unit _ => True | _,_ => False end
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ => match v1,v2 with
     | tm_inl a1 _, tm_inl a2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2
     | tm_inr b1 _, tm_inr b2 _ => val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
     | _,_ => False end
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ => match v1,v2 with
     | tm_pair a1 b1 _, tm_pair a2 b2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2 /\ val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
     | _,_ => False end
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
     value v1 -> value v2 ->
     forall (a1 a2 : tm) (r : label), value a1 -> value a2 -> val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2 ->
       flows_to (join (security_of T).(reader) p) r ->
       forall u1 u2, evaluates (tm_app v1 a1 r) u1 -> evaluates (tm_app v2 a2 r) u2 ->
       val_rel l (join (security_of T).(indirect_reader) p) T2 u1 u2
  end.

Consider c = tm_inl (tm_unit public) high_security where high_security = {reader=High, ir=High}. Type of c via T_Inl with κ=high_security: Ty_Sum (Ty_Unit public)(Ty_Unit public) high_security. To get type with k=public, use T_Sub: need security_le high_security public = flows_to High Low ∧ ... = False. So no.

What if c is a variable x : Ty_Sum ... public, substituted by t1? In the theorem, the hole x has type T_secret with T_secret.ir=High. Could T_secret = Ty_Sum (Ty_Unit public)(Ty_Unit public) public? Then security_of T_secret .ir = Low, contradicting the hypothesis (which forces T_secret.ir=High). So the hole's type can't be a public sum. But the context C could contain a function f : Arrow T_secret' ... applied to something... Hmm, the condition c is a subterm typed in context [x:T_secret]; it could be `x` itself only if T_secret is the sum type with k = T_secret's security, ir=High. Then k.ir=High; the value annotation k1 of t1's evaluation: can t1 : T_secret evaluate to inl v k1 with k1.ir > High? No, High is top. So k1.ir ≤ High = k.ir. OK.

What if c is an application whose result type has security k, but the actual function returns a value with bigger annotation? E.g., C contains a function g : Arrow T1 (Ty_Sum ... public) κ_g where the function body is tm_inl unit SECRET with SECRET = {High,High}? The body's type must be ≤ the declared codomain via subtyping. T_Abs's body is typed at T2 (the codomain) exactly; the abs's declared codomain is whatever the type says. To return an inl with annotation High as a value of type sum public, the body's typing would need T_Sub at the body level: has_type ... (inl unit high) (sum public) uses T_Sub requiring security_le high public = False. So not typable. So typing does constrain annotations. The side condition is a semantic reflection of that.

But could the value come from a variable substitution at a *different* type with a weaker security? E.g., in an environment, a variable y : T_y is substituted by a value with annotation ≤ T_y's security (by the env relation at the time of extension). In the fundamental lemma, env extensions happen at binder applications where we extend with w1,w2 related at T1 via val_rel, whose side condition gives annotation ≤ T1's protection (Low). So yes, values in the env satisfy their types' annotation bounds — provided the initial env does. The initial env maps x to the actual secret terms t1,t2 whose relation is assumed (interp), but the actual values from evaluating t1,t2 are only constrained by val_rel at T_secret, whose obs fails, so the side condition is vacuous! Hmm, in the theorem, T_secret has ir=High so obs fails and we get no annotation bound on t1's values. But that's fine: wherever the hole's type is used, the *type* T_secret's security has ir=High, so any uses of the value in eliminations (case/app/fst) produce results with protection ≥ ... and the if/case on the hole type with k.ir=High means all is secret; the analysis then doesn't require bounds because we can raise protection to High. But if a subterm's type is derived from T_secret via subtyping, security_le keeps ir High? Subtyping from T_secret to U requires security_le (security_of T_secret)(security_of U), so U.ir ≥ High = High. So all uses of the hole carry ir=High. The problematic T_If requires the condition's type to be exactly Ty_Sum (Ty_Unit public)(Ty_Unit public) k with k as a *type variable*; if the condition is related to the hole, k.ir would be High, so protections are fine.

So maybe the side condition is needed only in some cases, but it's easier to prove uniformly.

Now the env relation definition and its properties:

Definition env_rel (l : label) (Gamma : context) (sigma1 sigma2 : atom -> tm) : Prop :=
  (forall y : atom, locally_closed (sigma1 y) /\ locally_closed (sigma2 y)) /\
  (forall y T, lookup_context y Gamma = Some T -> interp l Low T (sigma1 y) (sigma2 y)).

We also need in the fundamental lemma (T_Abs/T_Case binder extension):
- lc for the extended sigma: given lc of w (values) and lc of previous.
- interp at x: interp l Low T1 w1 w2 from val_rel + value.
  Lemma val_rel_interp: value v1 -> value v2 -> val_rel l p T v1 v2 -> interp l p T v1 v2.
  Proof: unfold interp; intros u1 u2 [Hm1 Hv1] [Hm2 Hv2]; multi_value Hm1 Hval1 gives u1 = v1; rewrite; same for u2; assumption.
  Requires multi_value: multi v u -> value v -> u = v.
- interp at other y: lookup_context y (update Gamma x T1) = Some T with y ≠ x... but what if y = x and also lookup gives the old value? If y = x, lookup (update Gamma x T1) x = Some T1 (regardless), so T = T1. Since lookup is deterministic (we need a lemma: lookup_context y (update Gamma x T) = Some U -> if y = x then U = T). Then interp at x. If y ≠ x, lookup y (update Gamma x T1) = lookup y Gamma, use env_rel.
  So we need a lookup lemma: lookup_context x (update Gamma x T) = Some T; and lookup_context y (update Gamma x T) = lookup_context y Gamma for y ≠ x. Prove with Nat.eqb lemmas (atoms are nat).

The fundamental lemma statement:

Lemma fundamental : forall Gamma t T, has_type Gamma t T ->
  forall l sigma1 sigma2, env_rel l Gamma sigma1 sigma2 ->
  interp l Low T (subst_fn sigma1 t)(subst_fn sigma2 t).

Induction on has_type. We'll need the T_Var case to use env_rel; T_Abs/T_Case with fresh x.

subst_fn:
Fixpoint subst_fn (sigma : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar y => sigma y
  | tm_unit s => tm_unit s
  | tm_abs T body s => tm_abs T (subst_fn sigma body) s

Now subst_fn_fix_on:
Lemma subst_fn_fix_on : forall (sigma : atom -> tm) (t : tm),
  (forall y, In y (fv t) -> sigma y = tm_fvar y) -> subst_fn sigma t = t.
Proof.
  intros sigma t H. transitivity (subst_fn (fun x => tm_fvar x) t).
  - apply subst_fn_ext. exact H.
  - apply subst_fn_id.
Qed.

Let me define:

Definition vsec (v : tm) : security :=
  match v with
  | tm_unit k => k
  | tm_abs _ _ k => k
  | tm_pair _ _ k => k
  | tm_inl _ k => k
  | tm_inr _ k => k
  | _ => public
  end.

Definition obs (l p : label) (T : ty) : Prop :=
  flows_to (join (security_of T).(indirect_reader) p) l.

Fixpoint val_rel (l p : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  obs l p T ->
  security_le (vsec v1) (protect_security (security_of T) p) /\
  security_le (vsec v2) (protect_security (security_of T) p) /\
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit _ =>
      match v1, v2 with tm_unit _, tm_unit _ => True | _, _ => False end
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 _ =>
      match v1, v2 with
      | tm_inl a1 _, tm_inl a2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2
      | tm_inr b1 _, tm_inr b2 _ => val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
      | _, _ => False
      end
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 _ =>
      match v1, v2 with
      | tm_pair a1 b1 _, tm_pair a2 b2 _ =>
          val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2 /\ val_rel l Low T2 b1 b2
      | _, _ => False
      end
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 _ =>
      value v1 -> value v2 ->
      forall (a1 a2 : tm) (r : label),
        value a1 -> value a2 -> val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2 ->
        flows_to (join (security_of T).(reader) p) r ->
        forall u1 u2 : tm,
          evaluates (tm_app v1 a1 r) u1 ->
          evaluates (tm_app v2 a2 r) u2 ->
          val_rel l (join (security_of T).(indirect_reader) p) T2 u1 u2
  end.

Definition interp (l p : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> val_rel l p T v1 v2.

Fixpoint val_rel (l p : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) {struct T} : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit s =>
      flows_to (join s.(indirect_reader) p) l ->
      security_le (vsec v1) (protect_security s p) /\
      security_le (vsec v2) (protect_security s p) /\
      match v1, v2 with tm_unit _, tm_unit _ => True | _, _ => False end
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to (join s.(indirect_reader) p) l ->
      security_le (vsec v1) (protect_security s p) /\
      security_le (vsec v2) (protect_security s p) /\
      match v1, v2 with
      | tm_inl a1 _, tm_inl a2 _ => val_rel l Low T1 a1 a2

multi_protect_value:
Lemma multi_protect_value : forall (L : label) (t w : tm),
  multi t w -> value w -> multi (tm_protect L t) (protect_value w L).
Proof.
  intros L t w Hm. induction Hm as [| t1 t2 t3 Hstep Hmulti IH]; intros Hw.
  - eapply multi_step; [apply ST_ProtectValue; exact Hw | apply multi_refl].
  - eapply multi_step; [apply ST_Protect; exact Hstep | apply IH; exact Hw].
Qed.

  Lemma env_rel_extend : forall (l : label) (Gamma : context) (x : atom) (T1 : ty)
      (sigma1 sigma2 : atom -> tm) (w1 w2 : tm),
    env_rel l Gamma sigma1 sigma2 ->
    val_rel l Low T1 w1 w2 ->
    value w1 -> value w2 ->
    env_rel l (update Gamma x T1)
      (fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then w1 else sigma1 y)
      (fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then w2 else sigma2 y).
  Proof:
    intros l Gamma x T1 sigma1 sigma2 w1 w2 [Hlc Henv] Hvr Hw1 Hw2. split.

Theorem noninterference : forall (C : program_context) (t1 t2 : tm)
    (T_secret T_result : ty),
  has_type empty t1 T_secret ->
  has_type empty t2 T_secret ->
  context_has_type C T_secret T_result ->
  ground T_result ->
  transparent T_result ->
  ~ flows_to (security_of T_secret).(indirect_reader)
      (security_of T_result).(indirect_reader) ->
  same_result (plug C t1) (plug C t2).
Proof.
  intros C t1 t2 T_secret T_result Ht1 Ht2 Hctx Hgr Htr Hni.
  destruct (not_flows_to _ _ Hni) as [Hsec Hres].
  rewrite Hres in Hni.
  destruct Hctx as [L Hctx].
  pose (x := fresh_from (L ++ fv_context C)).
  assert (HxL : ~ In x L).
  { unfold x. intro Hin. apply (fresh_from_notin (L ++ fv_context C)).
    apply in_or_app. left. exact Hin. }
  assert (Hxfv : ~ In x (fv_context C)).
  { unfold x. intro Hin. apply (fresh_from_notin (L ++ fv_context C)).
    apply in_or_app. right. exact Hin. }
  assert (HtyC : has_type (update empty x T_secret) (plug C (tm_fvar x)) T_result).
  { apply Hctx. exact HxL. }
  pose (s1 := fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then t1 else tm_fvar y).
  pose (s2 := fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then t2 else tm_fvar y).
  assert (Henv : env_rel Low (update empty x T_secret) s1 s2).
  { split.
    - intros y. unfold s1, s2. destruct (Nat.eqb y x).
      + split; apply has_type_lc; assumption.
      + split; exact I.
    - intros y T Hlook. apply lookup_update_some in Hlook.
      destruct Hlook as [[E1 E2] | [Hne Hlook]].
      + subst y. subst T. unfold s1, s2. rewrite Nat.eqb_refl. simpl.
        intros v1 v2 He1 He2.
        apply val_rel_vacuous_gen. rewrite join_low_r. exact Hni.
      + exfalso. unfold empty in Hlook. simpl in Hlook. discriminate Hlook. }
  pose proof (fundamental (update empty x T_secret) (plug C (tm_fvar x)) T_result
                HtyC Low s1 s2 Henv) as Hfin.
  assert (Eplug1 : subst_fn s1 (plug C (tm_fvar x)) = plug C t1).
  { rewrite (subst_fn_plug C (tm_fvar x) s1).
    - intros y Hy. unfold s1. destruct (Nat.eqb y x) eqn:E.
      + apply Nat.eqb_eq in E. subst y. exfalso. apply Hxfv. exact Hy.
      + reflexivity.
    - unfold s1. simpl. rewrite Nat.eqb_refl. reflexivity. }
  assert (Eplug2 : subst_fn s2 (plug C (tm_fvar x)) = plug C t2).
  { rewrite (subst_fn_plug C (tm_fvar x) s2).
    - intros y Hy. unfold s2. destruct (Nat.eqb y x) eqn:E.
      + apply Nat.eqb_eq in E. subst y. exfalso. apply Hxfv. exact Hy.
      + reflexivity.
    - unfold s2. simpl. rewrite Nat.eqb_refl. reflexivity. }
  rewrite Eplug1, Eplug2 in Hfin.
  unfold same_result. intros v1 v2 He1 He2.
  apply (val_rel_erase Low T_result v1 v2 Hgr).
  - eapply transparent_all_below.
    + exact Htr.
    + rewrite Hres. apply flows_to_refl.
  - apply Hfin; assumption.
Qed.
